N-D10.question: Which ClickHouse column holds the country code of a location, and what is its type?

N-S1.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I list the financial amounts per year together with the name of the company?
N-S1.expected: Join pg.companyfinancials.companyid -> pg.company.companyid. Final: pg.companyfinancials.year, pg.companyfinancials.amount, pg.companyfinancials.currency, and pg.company.fullname and pg.company.entityname (owner 2026-10-18: either is fine; a good answer mentions both)

N-S2.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I get the technologies used by a company together with the company website?
N-S2.expected: Join pg.companytechnographics.companyid -> pg.company.companyid. Final: pg.companytechnographics.technologyname, pg.company.website

N-S3.question: In ClickHouse, how do I get from a person's name to the job titles and the names of the companies they hold them at?
N-S3.expected: Join ch.Experience.personID -> ch.Person.personID and ch.Experience.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID. Final: ch.Person.name, ch.Experience.jobTitle and ch.Experience.title (owner: mention both), ch.Company.companyName

N-S4.question: In ClickHouse, how do I get the free email column for the people who worked at a given company?
N-S4.expected: Join ch.Experience.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID, then ch.Experience.personID -> ch.PersonContact.personID. Final: ch.PersonContact.freeMails, ch.Company.companyName

N-S5.question: In ClickHouse, how do I list the city of each company location together with the industry names of that company?
N-S5.expected: Join ch.Location.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID; ch.CompanyIndustry.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID; ch.CompanyIndustry.industryID -> ch.Industry.industryID. Final: ch.Location.City, ch.Industry.name (or displayName)

N-S6.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I get the contact strings of companies together with the industry names of those companies?
N-S6.expected: Join pg.companycontact.companyid -> pg.companyindustry.companyid, then pg.companyindustry.classificationid -> pg.industryclassification.classificationid. Final: pg.companycontact.contactstring, pg.companycontact.contacttype, pg.industryclassification.name

N-S7.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I list the people with a company experience record together with the company name?
N-S7.expected: Join pg.companyexperience.personid -> pg.person.personid and pg.companyexperience.companyid -> pg.company.companyid. Final: pg.person.name, pg.companyexperience.role, pg.company.fullname and pg.company.entityname (owner: mention both)

N-S8.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I get the relation type of each company relation together with the industry names of the company?
N-S8.expected: Join pg.companyrelation.companyid -> pg.companyindustry.companyid, then pg.companyindustry.classificationid -> pg.industryclassification.classificationid. Final: pg.companyrelation.relationtype, pg.industryclassification.name

N-S9.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I list the investors of each investment round of a company with the company name and round amount?
N-S9.expected: Join pg.companyinvestmentround.companyid -> pg.company.companyid and pg.companyinvestor.investmentid -> pg.companyinvestmentround.investmentid. Final: pg.company.fullname, pg.companyinvestmentround.amount, pg.companyinvestor.surfaceform and pg.companyinvestor.summary (owner: both describe the investor). The investor company id column (investorcompanyid) must NOT be joined to pg.company.companyid (listed FALSE)

N-S10.question: In PostgreSQL, how do I get the employee category of companies located in a given city?
N-S10.expected: Join pg.companyemployeecategory.companyid -> pg.location.companyid. Final: pg.location.city, pg.companyemployeecategory.category (optionally pg.companyemployeecategory.empcatid)

N-C1.question: List every column in both databases that holds a part of a postal address.
N-C1.expected: pg.location: street, city, region, country, postalcode, addressfull (all text; latitude, longitude, precision are coordinates, not address parts). ch.Location: Street, City, State, CountryCode, Zip (all Nullable(String))

N-C2.question: Which PostgreSQL tables have a confidence column?
N-C2.expected: pg.companycontact, companyemployeecategory, companyexperience, companyfinancials, companyinvestmentround, companyinvestor, companyrelation, companytechnographics, industryclassification, person (all text). pg.company has metadata_confidence, not confidence. companyindustry and location have none

N-C3.question: List every column in the catalogue that holds a person's name or a part of it.
N-C3.expected: pg.person.name; pg.companyexperience.personname; pg.company.foundername; pg.company.ceoname; ch.Person.name, firstName, middleInitial, lastName

N-C4.question: Which columns in the catalogue have a timestamp or datetime type, and in which tables?
N-C4.expected: pg: created_at (timestamp without time zone) in all 13 tables. ch: _version (Nullable(DateTime)) in all 7 tables. pg._version is integer, not a timestamp

N-C5.question: List every column in both databases that holds a money amount or the currency of one.
N-C5.expected: pg.company.totalinvestment (bigint), pg.company.totalinvestmentcurrency (text), pg.companyfinancials.amount (bigint), pg.companyfinancials.currency (text), pg.companyinvestmentround.amount (bigint), pg.companyinvestmentround.currency (text); ch.Company.companyRevenueIn000s (Nullable(Int64)), companyRevenue (Nullable(String)), companyRevenueRange (Nullable(String)), companyRevenue_currency (Nullable(String))

N-C6.question: Which columns, other than version columns, have a numeric type in PostgreSQL?
N-C6.expected: pg.company.totalinvestment (bigint), pg.companyfinancials.year (integer), pg.companyfinancials.amount (bigint), pg.companyinvestmentround.amount (bigint). Everything else is text or timestamp

N-C7.question: Which ClickHouse columns are not nullable, and what do they have in common?
N-C7.expected: ch.Company.companyID, ch.CompanyIndustry.companyID, ch.CompanyIndustry.industryID, ch.Experience.personID, ch.Experience.companyID, ch.Industry.industryID, ch.Location.locationID, ch.Person.personID, ch.PersonContact.freeMails; all String; mostly ids

N-C8.question: List every column in both databases that links people to companies or to person records.
N-C8.expected: pg.companyexperience.personid, pg.companyexperience.companyid; pg.person.personid; ch.Experience.personID, ch.Experience.companyID; ch.Person.personID; ch.PersonContact.personID. Confirmed TRUE: pg.companyexperience.personid -> pg.person.personid; ch.Experience.personID -> ch.Person.personID and -> ch.PersonContact.personID; ch.Experience.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID

N-C9.question: In every source, which tables hold a role, title or category of a person or employees?

N-C10.question: Which tables in both databases describe locations of companies, and which columns carry the company id?
N-C10.expected: pg.location (companyid, locationid); ch.Location (companyID Nullable(Int64), locationID String). Confirmed TRUE: pg.location.companyid -> pg.company.companyid, ch.Location.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID

N-I1.question: Can I match PostgreSQL location rows to ClickHouse Location rows on their location ids?
N-I1.expected: No. pg.location.locationid -> ch.Location.locationID is listed FALSE; the two databases share no ids

N-I2.question: Is pg.companyinvestor.investorcompanyid a reference to pg.company.companyid?
N-I2.expected: No. Listed FALSE; the catalogue cannot say which table the investor company id refers to (no investor company table)

N-I3.question: Can I find the ClickHouse person for a PostgreSQL company experience record via personid?
N-I3.expected: No. pg.companyexperience.personid -> ch.Person.personID (and ch.Experience, ch.PersonContact) is listed FALSE; use pg.person within PostgreSQL only

N-I4.question: Between ch.Experience.jobTitle and ch.Experience.title, which should I use for a person's job title?
N-I4.expected: Both are Nullable(String) in the same table; the catalogue does not state the difference. A good answer lists both, says the difference cannot be established from names and types, and suggests title might be a shorter or alternate form only as a guess

N-I5.question: Between pg.company.entityname, fullname and description, which column holds the company's name?
N-I5.expected: entityname and fullname are both text name candidates; description is a free-text description, not a name. Which is canonical cannot be established

N-I6.question: In the pg.company and pg.location relationship on companyid, which table is the parent?
N-I6.expected: Cannot be established. Both pg.company.companyid -> pg.location.companyid and pg.location.companyid -> pg.company.companyid are listed TRUE; companyid is the shared key. pg.company is the natural entity table by its columns

N-I7.question: Does the catalogue tell me which company is the parent and which is the subsidiary in pg.companyrelation?
N-I7.expected: Cannot be established. The columns are companyid, relatedcompanyid, relationtype (text), types, summary. Direction is not stated. Also pg.companyrelation.relatedcompanyid -> pg.company.companyid is listed FALSE, so that column is not a confirmed reference to pg.company

N-I8.question: Which PostgreSQL column holds a person's email address?
N-I8.expected: No dedicated person email column exists: pg.person has name, role, summary, types, confidence only. pg.companycontact.contactstring with contacttype is attached to companies, not to persons. The catalogue cannot establish that either holds a person's email

N-I9.question: Can I tell which ClickHouse Location row is a company's current location?
N-I9.expected: No. ch.Location has no current or primary flag (columns: Zip, companyID, Street, CountryCode, locationID, State, City, _version). Only pg.location has iscurrent and isprimary (text), and those cannot be applied to ClickHouse because the databases share no ids

N-I10.question: In ClickHouse, how can I find the company name for a row in PersonContact?
N-I10.expected: PersonContact has no company id (columns: freeMails, personID, _version). Go two hops: ch.PersonContact.personID -> ch.Experience.personID, then ch.Experience.companyID -> ch.Company.companyID; final ch.Company.companyName. A person may have several experience rows
